title: Responding in Defender XDR (3): Incidents, UEBA, Security Copilot and Complex Attacks

header.html: Investigate and remediate alerts and incidents identified by Microsoft Sentinel; investigate incidents by using agentic AI, including embedded Microsoft Security Copilot; investigate complex attacks, such as multi-stage, multi-domain and lateral movement; manage security incidents by using case management
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Managing incidents (case management)

Item Fact
Incident page tabs Attack story, Alerts, Activities, Assets, Investigations, Evidence and Response, Summary, Similar incidents
Assets Devices, Users, Mailboxes, Apps, Cloud resources
Status Active (default), In progress, Resolved (needs a resolution note; also resolves linked active alerts)
Classification Not set, True positive (with threat type), Informational, expected activity (security tests, red team, expected behavior), False positive
Owner One user or group
Tags Custom tags and system tags (attack type, automatic investigation or disruption, Defender Experts, critical assets)
Comments Up to 30,000 characters each, kept in the Activities log
Tasks A checklist for the incident; created by hand or by a Sentinel automation rule

Incident cases (preview, the recommended experience) are found under Cases > Incident. A case has an overview with a Copilot summary and attack graph, plus Alerts, Assets, Investigations, Evidence, Activities, Similar cases and Comments and attachments. Alerts can be moved between cases. Permissions: Security Data Read to view, Security Data Manage to change.

Exam tip

. Resolve with a classification. A sanctioned penetration test is Informational, expected activity, not false positive.

2Investigating complex attacks

A multi-stage, multi-domain attack touches several products. Defender XDR correlates alerts from endpoint, email, identity, cloud apps and cloud workloads into one incident.

Tool What it shows
Alert story What happened, Actions taken, Related events
Incident graph Entities and alerts over time; filter by severity, status and service source; hide entity types
Go hunt All activity, Related alerts, All user anomalies (preview, last 30 days, needs UEBA)
Blast radius The top 8 attack paths from a selected node to critical targets

Blast radius extends and replaces attack path analysis. Prerequisites: Sentinel data lake onboarding and Exposure management (read). Path limits: up to 7 hops from the source, 5 hops in cloud, 5 on-premises and 3 hybrid. It shows possible paths, not guaranteed ones, and only nodes inside your RBAC scope.

Exam tip

. Lateral movement = follow the incident graph from the first compromised device to the next. Blast radius = what the attacker could reach next.

3Investigating Sentinel incidents

You need Microsoft Sentinel Responder (guest users who assign incidents also need Directory Reader).

Feature Fact
Overview Incident timeline, Similar incidents (up to 20), Entities, Top insights
Entities tab Info, Timeline (previous 7 days of alerts, bookmarks, anomalies), Insights
Investigation graph Needs entity mappings; works for incidents up to 30 days old; has exploration queries and a parallel timeline
Buttons Tasks, Activity log, Logs; actions Run playbook, Create automation rule
Comments 30,000 characters each, 100 per incident; only the author edits; delete needs Sentinel Contributor

4User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA)

UEBA builds behavioral baselines and scores anomalies. Enable it in the Defender portal: System > Settings > Microsoft Sentinel > UEBA, turn on UEBA, sync Active Directory (needs Defender for Identity) and Microsoft Entra ID, then turn on Anomalies. There is no license cost, only storage.

Table Content
IdentityInfo Entity profiles from Entra and optionally AD
BehaviorAnalytics Deviations and InvestigationPriority (0 to 10, event level, near real time)
UserPeerAnalytics Top 20 peers per user
Anomalies AnomalyScore (0 to 1, behavior level, batch)

5Security Copilot and agentic AI

Microsoft Security Copilot is embedded in the Defender portal and gives generative AI help during an investigation.

Embedded capability Use
Summarize incidents Summary of up to 100 alerts; cached for one week
Guided response Suggested next actions
Analyze files and scripts Explains what a file or script does
Generate KQL queries for hunting Natural language to KQL
Create incident reports, summarize devices and identities Reports and asset summaries

Agents work on their own for a defined task: Security Alert Triage Agent (phishing and other alert triage, preview), Threat Intelligence Briefing Agent, Threat Hunting Assistant, Security Analyst Agent, Dynamic Threat Detection Agent. For Entra: Conditional Access Optimization Agent and Identity Risk Management Agent. Agents are not enabled automatically; each is set up (often by a Security Administrator).

Licensing and roles Fact
Included capacity Microsoft 365 E5 and E7: 400 security compute units (SCUs) per month per 1,000 paid licenses, up to 10,000 per month; resets monthly, no rollover
Other customers Provision 1 to 100 SCUs, billed hourly
Copilot roles Security Copilot Owner (capacity, usage, data sharing) and Contributor (sessions, promptbooks); these are Copilot roles, not Entra roles
Embedded access Also needs the product role (for example a unified RBAC role with Security Copilot permission)
Exam tip

. Copilot summarizes and suggests; the analyst decides. Agents must be set up. SCUs measure usage and E5 includes a monthly allowance.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An incident came from a sanctioned red team exercise. How should the analyst close it?

  • AResolve it as informational, expected activity, with security test selected
  • BResolve it as false positive, because no real attacker was involved
  • CResolve it as true positive, with the threat type set to malware
  • DLeave it active until the exercise report is published to the team
Show the answer

Answer: A. Sanctioned tests are classified as Informational, expected activity with the activity type for security tests.

S2An analyst must trace how an attacker moved from a phished mailbox to a server across several products. Which tool gives the best view?

  • AThe Analytics rule templates tab in Sentinel
  • BThe Tenant Allow/Block List in the mail flow rules
  • CThe device inventory page filtered by operating system
  • DThe Attack story and incident graph of the incident
Show the answer

Answer: D. The attack story and incident graph show correlated alerts and entities across domains over time.

S3A SOC wants to use blast radius in an incident. Which two prerequisites apply?

  • ADefender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Safe Links enabled
  • BA Sentinel data lake onboarding and Exposure management (read)
  • CA custom detection rule and a Logic App playbook in place
  • DEntra ID P2 and a risk-based Conditional Access policy
Show the answer

Answer: B. Blast radius uses the Sentinel data lake and graph and needs Exposure management (read) or higher.

S4An analyst wants a numeric priority from 0 to 10 for unusual user activity in Sentinel. Which table holds it?

  • AIdentityInfo, which holds entity profiles
  • BUserPeerAnalytics, which holds peer groups
  • CSecurityIncident, which holds incident records
  • DBehaviorAnalytics, which holds InvestigationPriority
Show the answer

Answer: D. BehaviorAnalytics has the InvestigationPriority score from 0 to 10.

S5An organization has Microsoft 365 E5 and 5,000 paid licenses. How much Security Copilot capacity is included per month?

  • A2,000 security compute units, from 400 per 1,000 licenses
  • B400 security compute units, regardless of license count
  • C10,000 security compute units for every customer
  • DNone, because E5 customers must provision all the capacity themselves
Show the answer

Answer: A. E5 includes 400 SCUs per 1,000 licenses per month, so 5,000 licenses give 2,000.

S6The investigation graph button does not work for a Sentinel incident. What are likely causes?

  • AThe incident has no entity mappings or is older than 30 days
  • BThe incident is a false positive and the graph is disabled
  • CThe incident belongs to Defender for Office 365 and has no alerts
  • DThe incident is owned by a user who has the Reader role
Show the answer

Answer: A. The graph needs entity mappings and supports incidents up to 30 days old.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which classification fits a sanctioned penetration test?

Show the answer

Informational, expected activity.

R2How many attack paths does blast radius show?

Show the answer

The top 8.

R3Which role investigates Sentinel incidents?

Show the answer

Microsoft Sentinel Responder.

R4What is the range of InvestigationPriority?

Show the answer

0 to 10.

R5What do E5 customers receive per 1,000 licenses?

Show the answer

400 SCUs per month.

R6Are Security Copilot agents enabled automatically?

Show the answer

No, each must be set up.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Incident states Active, In progress, Resolved; classify before resolving
Attack story alert story plus incident graph; Go hunt
Blast radius top 8 paths; Sentinel data lake and Exposure management (read)
Sentinel investigation Responder; graph needs entity mappings, 30 days
UEBA IdentityInfo, BehaviorAnalytics (0 to 10), UserPeerAnalytics, Anomalies (0 to 1)
Copilot summary of 100 alerts, KQL generation, agents set up by hand; E5: 400 SCUs per 1,000 licenses
